attempts.label: DANDI:001201
attempts.paper_title: Long-term Intracortical Neural activity and Kinematics (LINK): An intracortical neural dataset for chronic brain-machine interfaces, neuroscience, and machine learning
attempts.entry_title: Long-term intracortical neural activity and kinematics, LINK (Temmar et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held up in this data: signal power, active channel count and dimensionality decline over the years, most channels keep their tuning, same-day decoding stays stable with the LSTM ahead of ridge regression, cross-day accuracy drops sharply then levels off, and multi-day training softens the early drop. Population drift held up only in part. The text's tuning by array came out reversed with the files' array labels, though it matches the paper's own figure panels. The long-term decay fits failed, likely because only 12 of 283 starting sessions could be run, and daily fine-tuning was too costly to test. One supplementary slope came out with the opposite sign.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Temmar et al. (2025) on dandiset 001201, which holds 312 sessions of spiking-band power, threshold crossings and finger kinematics from one macaque over 3.5 years. It checks the dataset's counts and contents, the decline of neural signals over time, single-channel tuning, same-day and cross-day decoding with ridge regression and an LSTM, and multi-day training. The LSTM analyses run on subsets of sessions for time, and the continual fine-tuning is too large to run.

notebooks.title: The dataset, neural signals and tuning over time (Figures 2, 3, S2, S4, S5)
Same-day and cross-day decoding (Figure 4, Appendix C.1)
Multi-day training (Figure 5A; Figure 5B is not run)
LSTM decoding in July to November 2022 (fig2a-irregular-shifts, after round 2)

outcomes.statement: The dataset holds 312 sessions recorded on 303 days spanning 1,242 days, two sessions (one CO, one RD) on 9 days, each session 375 successful trials, from days 349 to 1591 after implant.
outcomes.source: Section 3, The LINK Dataset, paragraph 1 (page 4); Appendix B.1 and B.2; Appendix A.2
outcomes.quote: on 303 days spanning 1,242 days. The dataset comprises 312 ’sessions’ of 375 (mostly) contiguous trial acquisitions. Each session contains one of two variations to the task, ‘center-out’ or ‘random’, described below. On 9 days, two sessions are available as both tasks were performed.
outcomes.notes: 312 session files on 303 dates, 2020-01-27 to 2023-06-22, a span of 1242 days. On 9 dates there are two files, each a CO and an RD session. Every session has 375 trials. The days after implant (349 to 1591) were not compared, as the criterion asks only when the dataset gives the implant date; it gives the date of birth (2012-05-26) and no implant date.

outcomes.statement: Each session holds SBP and TCR for 96 motor-cortex channels and the position and velocity of the two finger groups in 20 ms bins, with per-trial target positions, start times, lengths and target style, and per-channel array locations and impedances.
outcomes.source: Section 3, The LINK Dataset, paragraph 1 (page 4); Section 3.3; Appendix B.3
outcomes.quote: In each session, we provide neural data preprocessed into two neural features in 20ms bins... spiking-band power (SBP) and threshold crossing rate (TCR). We also provide the position and velocity of the 2DOF at the same resolution.
outcomes.notes: All 312 files hold 96-channel SpikingBandPower and ThresholdCrossings and the four kinematic series on one timestamp vector, the trials columns of Appendix B.3, and electrodes with array, bank, row and column. 81 files have no imp column (14 in 2020, 2 in 2021, 49 in 2022, 16 in 2023). Appendix A.2 says no impedances are reported for a session without a measurement within three weeks, so this may be the documented behaviour, but the criterion asks for the column in every file. Within runs the timestamps step 0.019 to 0.021 s; 29 sessions have 72 pauses of 1.05 to 472.9 s. Velocity at bin t equals position at t+1 minus position at t in every bin except the 72 bins before a pause, a forward difference.
deviations: The criterion's velocity check, against the difference of consecutive binned positions, is shown both ways; the data match the forward difference, not the backward one.

outcomes.statement: The monkey's real-time task performance, measured as average Fitts' law throughput per day, appears to improve gradually over the dataset.
outcomes.quote: In S2, we show the average throughput across all trials for each day, and noted that Monkey N’s performance appears to gradually improve throughout the course of the dataset.
outcomes.notes: Daily mean throughput rises under all three readings, (a) 0.238 bits/s per year (r = 0.31, p = 5.8e-08), (b) 0.068 (p = 7.7e-37), (c) 0.455 (p = 2.8e-20), over 303 days. Under (a) the yearly means are 3.66, 3.96, 4.33 and 3.85 for 2020 to 2023. 998 trials whose length is at most the 750 ms hold get no throughput under (a) and (c).
deviations: Throughput's formula is cited to Nason et al. 2021 and not given in the paper or its code; the three readings of the criterion are run and agree.
The first trial of each session, whose starting targets are not in the file, has no throughput.
The p < 0.05 threshold is the criterion's standard choice; the paper gives no test.

outcomes.statement: Average SBP across channels decreased gradually by about 0.033 microvolts per month, as estimated by a linear model fit to every channel's mean SBP on every day.
outcomes.quote: Average SBP across channels decreased gradually by approximately 0.033 μV per month, as estimated by a linear model.
outcomes.notes: With the stored values (microvolts by their conversion factor), the fit to 29,088 channel-day means gives -1.110e-03 per day, -0.0338 per month, inside -0.033 +- 0.0033. Reading (a), the stored values times 0.25, gives -0.0084 per month. The code's converter divides the stored SBP by 0.25 and its analysis multiplies by 0.25, so the code's path is reading (b).
deviations: The unit of SBP was open between two readings named in the criterion; reading (b) matches and (a) does not.

outcomes.statement: Groups of channels show irregular SBP shifts in some periods, for example from about July to November 2022, and these shifts did not affect overall decoding performance.
outcomes.quote: There are periods where groups of channels exhibit irregular shifts (e.g. ~2022-07 to ~2022-11), but these did not affect overall decoding performance.
outcomes.notes: Under the criterion's rule 38 of 42 days in July to November 2022 have at least five channels shifting on the same day (up to 66), so the shift part holds; but the rule flags 237 of the 243 other days that have a 30-day baseline, so it does not single out that period (0.974 of window days and 0.975 of other days have five or more; median 17 shifting channels a day in the window against 20 outside; with the 30 preceding recording days as baseline, 0.952 against 0.903). RR's median same-day R2 in the window is 0.321 (45 sessions), inside its 10th to 90th percentile range of 0.220 to 0.360. In decoding.ipynb the LSTM's median over the 3 window sessions among the every-16th is 0.652, just above its 90th percentile of 0.651 over 20 sessions; adding the 3 window sessions among the 12 highest-RR sessions, a selection biased towards high R2, gives 0.659. window.ipynb trains the LSTM on 24 of the 42 other window sessions and refits the 20 every-16th sessions, whose 10th to 90th percentile range is the same as in decoding.ipynb (0.529 to 0.651; single session values are not printed side by side). The median over the 27 window sessions with an LSTM is 0.641, inside that range, so the LSTM part holds and with it both parts of the criterion. The pass is narrow (0.010 below the 90th percentile, 18 window sessions unfitted). In the window, 11 of the 27 sessions are above the 90th percentile and 1 below the 10th; against the 17 every-16th sessions outside the window (0.524 to 0.616) the median would be above the range, in the direction of better decoding, and with the percentiles over all 44 sessions fitted (0.541 to 0.665) it is inside. The LSTM's margin over RR is the same in the window as elsewhere (median 0.303 against 0.301). The outcome was partially_reproduced after round 2 and changed to reproduced after round 3 of the verification agreed.
deviations: The LSTM is trained on 20 of the 312 sessions (every 16th in date order, chosen before any result), for time; one fit takes 77 to 223 s with four at once, depending on the run (77 s in round 1, 207 to 223 s in round 2; decoding.ipynb prints this run's), so all 312 would take 1.7 to 4.8 hours of fitting, over the 60-minute limit of a notebook.
A day's 30-day baseline needs at least 3 earlier days; days with fewer have no shift count. This is a standard choice the criterion does not fix.

In window.ipynb the LSTM is trained on 24 of the 42 window sessions outside the every-16th, spread evenly in date order and chosen before any result, for time (44 fits with the 20 reference sessions, 11 rounds of four).

outcomes.statement: The number of active channels, those with mean TCR above 1 Hz on a day, appears to decrease over time.
outcomes.quote: During iBMI experiments, we can roughly estimate the number of active channels by counting those with mean TCR > 1 Hz, shown in Figure 2B. Note that this appears to decrease over time.
outcomes.notes: The daily count of channels above 1 Hz falls by 6.5 per year (slope -0.0177 per day, r = -0.39, p = 2.6e-12, 303 days), from a mean of 44.6 in the first 30 sessions to 25.9 in the last 30.

outcomes.statement: The participation ratio of the active channels' SBP decreased by about 0.07 per month, as estimated by a linear model.
outcomes.quote: a linear model estimated that PR decreased by ~0.07 PR per month
outcomes.notes: PR of the active channels falls by 0.0708 per month (p = 1.5e-08, 303 days), inside -0.07 +- 0.007. With every session as a point, -0.0720.

outcomes.statement: Generally, 10 dimensions were sufficient to capture the majority of the variance of the active channels.
outcomes.quote: Generally, 10 dimensions were sufficient to capture the majority of the variance in active channels
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a) the daily PR is at most 10 on 84.8% of days (median 7.86). Under (b) the top 10 PCs explain more than 50% on every day; under (c) more than 80% on 44.6% of days, which alone would not reproduce it.

outcomes.statement: Mean SBP decreases over time in each 32-channel bank, with lower overall activity and a shallower slope on the lateral bank (-0.58e-3) than on the two medial banks (-1.34e-3 and -1.40e-3), against -1.11e-3 for all channels.
outcomes.source: Appendix C.2, paragraph after Figure S3; Figure S4; Section 4.1, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The slopes of the best-fit lines for the Lateral, Medial 1, and Medial 2 groups were −0.58 × 10−3, −1.34 × 10−3, and −1.40 × 10−3 respectively. This is compared to −1.11 × 10−3 for the overall SBP. This is largely because the average SBP is generally higher on the medial arrays
outcomes.notes: With the stored values, slopes per day are -5.84e-04 (lateral, bank A), -1.34e-03 (bank B), -1.40e-03 (bank C) and -1.11e-03 (all), equal to the supplement's values to the printed digits; the lateral bank has the lowest mean SBP (2.19 against 2.55 and 3.57). Both fit readings give the same slopes, since every day has every channel. Under unit reading (a) each slope is a quarter of these.
deviations: Medial 1 and Medial 2 are taken as banks B and C, which the paper does not name; the two medial values match in that order.

outcomes.statement: Grouped per session into active and inactive channels by TCR, mean SBP of active channels declines faster (-1.29e-3) than all channels, while the slope for inactive channels is near zero (0.54e-3), and inactive channels have lower SBP.
outcomes.source: Appendix C.2, paragraph after Figure S3; Figure S5; Section 4.1, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The slopes of the best-fit lines here were −1.29 × 10−3, and 0.54 × 10−3. As might be expected, the slope for the inactive channels was near 0
outcomes.notes: With the stored values and channel-session points, active channels decline at -1.261e-03 per day, inside the tolerance of -1.29e-3, and inactive channels have the lower mean SBP (2.15 against 3.74). The inactive slope is -5.36e-04, the size of the supplement's 0.54e-3 with the opposite sign, so outside the tolerance. The negative sign agrees with Section 4.1, which says all categories decreased. With session means (reading b) the slopes are -1.162e-03 and -4.50e-04. The criterion reproduces the claim only when both slopes are within tolerance and names no partial outcome, so the inactive slope decides it. Whether the supplement's +0.54e-3 lost its minus sign is asked of a reader in questions/temmar-2025.yaml; against -0.54e-3 the claim would be reproduced.
deviations: Each session classifies its own channels and is one point in time; on the 9 two-session days both sessions are points.

outcomes.statement: In a PCA fit to SBP z-scored per channel across the whole dataset, the per-day and per-quarter centroids of the top 3 PCs move through PC space over time, while the standard deviation of the top 3 PCs per quarter changes little except in two quarters.
outcomes.source: Section 4.1, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 2D and legend; Appendix C.3
outcomes.quote: Visually, these centroids appear to move throughout the PCA space over time, and except for two quarters, the standard deviation of the top 3 PCs does not exhibit large changes.
outcomes.notes: The centroids move: the first and last quarters' centroids are 17.04 apart against a mean within-quarter SD of 2.02. Three quarters (2021Q1, 2022Q3, 2023Q2) have a 3-PC SD more than 25% from the median of 1.83, where the rule allows two; at 50%, two quarters (2021Q1 at 4.27, 2022Q3 at 2.80) stand out, as the paper's two exceptions would. 2020Q2 has one session. The failure is marginal, as 2023Q2 is 25.5% from the median.
deviations: The PCA is computed from per-session sums of the SBP and its products, which gives the same components as fitting scikit-learn's PCA to the concatenated, z-scored matrix of all bins.
The 3-PC standard deviation of a quarter is the root mean square of the three PCs' SDs, as the criterion's movement rule defines it.

outcomes.statement: Average neural trajectories in the top 3 PCs for the eight movement directions remain visually separable in both the first year (2020) and the last (2023) of the dataset.
outcomes.source: Section 4.1, paragraph 4; Figure 2E and legend; Appendix C.3
outcomes.quote: The trajectories shown remain visually separable at the beginning and end of the dataset.
outcomes.notes: Nearest-centroid classification of the 37-bin, 3-PC trajectories by direction gives 0.212 in 2020 (15,951 trials) and 0.220 in 2023 (16,511 trials), against 1/8 (binomial p below 1e-200), the majority-class rate (0.158 and 0.184) and permuted labels (0.125 and 0.114). The code's alignment gives 0.232 and 0.221 but drops 92,544 of 116,683 trials. Accuracy is well above chance but low in absolute terms.
deviations: The first trial of each session, with no previous target in the file, has no direction.

A trial whose 37-bin window runs past its end, or with no movement onset, is dropped (1,067 of 116,683 under the paper's alignment). The paper says trials were trimmed to 37 bins but not what was done with shorter ones; this is a standard choice.
The day's PCA is fit to both sessions concatenated on two-session days.

outcomes.statement: Channel 7 is strongly tuned to MRS flexion throughout the dataset, whereas channel 32 shows large shifts in tuning angle; both are active, with average TCR above 1 Hz across the dataset.
outcomes.quote: Channel 7 was strongly tuned to MRS flexion throughout the dataset, whereas channel 32 exhibited large shifts in tuning angle.
outcomes.notes: Channel 7, circular median angle 81.1 degrees, circular IQR 18.6 degrees, median strength 0.0245 (sixth of 96; median over channels 0.0070). Channel 32, circular IQR 146.9 degrees (sixth largest; median 46.9). Mean TCR 3.12 and 36.45 Hz.

outcomes.statement: Per-channel tuning angles generally appear consistent through the dataset; in most channels the circular IQR of tuning angle is small, so their tunings did not change much.
outcomes.source: Section 4.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3C, 3D and 3E; Discussion, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In most channels, the circular IQR of tuning angles was small, suggesting their tunings did not change much throughout the dataset.
outcomes.notes: Below 90 degrees (reading b), 77.1% of all channels and 77.4% of the 53 active ones; below 45 degrees (reading a), 47.9% and 45.3%. The outcome holds under the 90-degree reading only.
deviations: The criterion names two thresholds; the result holds under one of them, so it is reproduced as the criterion states, and depends on that reading.

outcomes.statement: Many channels have very low tuning strength throughout the arrays' lifespan, and such channels typically have low average TCR per day.
outcomes.source: Section 4.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3D; Figure S3; Appendix C.2, paragraph after Figure S3
outcomes.quote: many channels have very low tuning strengths throughout the lifespan of the arrays. Such channels also typically showed low average TCRs per day, as shown in Figure S3.
outcomes.notes: Spearman rho = 0.925 (p = 3e-41) between median tuning strength and median daily TCR over 96 channels; the 24 weakest channels have a median TCR of 0.40 Hz against 0.87 Hz (Mann-Whitney p = 5.3e-11).

outcomes.statement: Channels on the medial array are mainly tuned to MRS flexion, with some to IDX flexion, while channels on the lateral array are more tuned to extension of both fingers, so channels on the same array tend to have similar tuning angles.
outcomes.quote: it appears that channels in the medial array (see Figure 1) are mainly tuned to MRS flexion, with some IDX flexion, while channels in the lateral array are more tuned to extension of both DOF.
outcomes.notes: With the files' array labels, medial channels' circular medians cluster near -130 degrees (extension of both); 2 of 64 are in the flexion sector. Most lateral channels are tuned to flexion (about 12 to 88 degrees); 2 of 32 are in the extension sector. With the array names swapped the pattern is close to the paper's (81.2% of file-lateral channels in the flexion sector, 92.2% of file-medial channels in the extension sector), though more of the flexion channels lie near IDX flexion (17) than near MRS flexion (11). The files' labels agree with Figure S1 (the electrodes table gives channel 47 as Medial, bank B, row 5, column 5) and with Figure S4 (lowest SBP on the lateral bank), so the disagreement is between the files and this sentence of the paper, or a sign convention of the paper's tuning angles. The verifier reports that the panels of Figure 3E and Figure 3C show the files' pattern, so the sentence of Section 4.2 and the figure disagree; whether the claim should follow the figure is asked of a reader.
deviations: The swapped-label reading is shown as a variant and does not decide the outcome.

outcomes.statement: Same-day decoding accuracy (R2 averaged across the four outputs on the 75 hold-out trials) remains relatively stable over the dataset, with most shifts shared by RR and LSTM.
outcomes.source: Section 4.3, paragraph 1; Figure 4A and legend; Discussion, paragraphs 1 and 4
outcomes.quote: Within-day decoding accuracy remains relatively stable across time, and the majority of shifts in accuracy are reflected in both decoders
outcomes.notes: RR same-day R2 slope +0.0020 per year (p = 0.58, 312 sessions), LSTM +0.0064 per year (p = 0.56, 20 sessions); Pearson r between the two over the 20 sessions 0.582 (p = 0.007); over all 32 sessions with an LSTM, which add the 12 highest-RR sessions and are not a sample of the dataset, r = 0.807 (p = 2.4e-08). RR without input normalisation, as the code fits it, gives +0.0019 per year (p = 0.58). Median R2, RR 0.296, LSTM 0.591.
deviations: The LSTM is trained on 20 of the 312 sessions (every 16th in date order, chosen before any result), for time; one fit takes 77 to 223 s with four at once, depending on the run (77 s in round 1, 207 to 223 s in round 2; decoding.ipynb prints this run's), so all 312 would take 1.7 to 4.8 hours of fitting, over the 60-minute limit of a notebook.

The LSTM's training noise is 0.1 white per bin and 0.2 bias per sequence and channel, as the Methods and the criterion state; the code's train_model passes the two to add_training_noise in the other order, so the code adds a bias of 0.1 and white noise of 0.2.
Training windows are drawn without replacement per epoch, as the code's shuffled DataLoader does; history before the start of a segment is zero in the normalised data.

outcomes.statement: The LSTM outperformed ridge regression in same-day decoding on every day.
outcomes.quote: While the LSTM outperformed RR on every day, we noted that there were baseline shifts in decoding performance that impacted both decoders
outcomes.notes: LSTM above RR on 20 of 20 every-16th sessions, by 0.223 to 0.385, and on all 12 of the other sessions with the highest RR R2 (RR 0.390 to 0.467, LSTM higher by 0.182 to 0.300), 32 of 32 in all, so no extra seeds were needed. The 12 include the session with the highest RR R2 of all 312 (0.467). The other 280 sessions were not tested with the LSTM.
deviations: The LSTM is trained on 20 of the 312 sessions (every 16th in date order, chosen before any result), for time; one fit takes 77 to 223 s with four at once, depending on the run (77 s in round 1, 207 to 223 s in round 2; decoding.ipynb prints this run's), so all 312 would take 1.7 to 4.8 hours of fitting, over the 60-minute limit of a notebook.

The 12 sessions with the highest RR same-day R2 outside the 20 were added after round 1 of the verification, chosen by that rule before their LSTM result, as the sessions where the LSTM is likeliest to fall below RR.

outcomes.statement: Decoding of finger positions is more accurate than of velocities, and MRS predictions are more accurate than IDX predictions.
outcomes.quote: In general, the position accuracies of the two finger groups outperformed velocities, and MRS predictions outperformed IDX predictions, suggesting there may be more information regarding the MRS finger group in the neural data than IDX.
outcomes.notes: Median R2 for RR (312 sessions) IDX and MRS position 0.316 and 0.362, velocity 0.220 and 0.286; LSTM (20 sessions) 0.645 and 0.663, velocity 0.480 and 0.576. Per session, position above velocity for both fingers in 62.8% (RR) and 75.0% (LSTM), MRS above IDX for both in 50.6% and 60.0%.
deviations: The LSTM is trained on 20 of the 312 sessions (every 16th in date order, chosen before any result), for time; one fit takes 77 to 223 s with four at once, depending on the run (77 s in round 1, 207 to 223 s in round 2; decoding.ipynb prints this run's), so all 312 would take 1.7 to 4.8 hours of fitting, over the 60-minute limit of a notebook.

outcomes.statement: Decoders tested on hold-out sets of other days within 100 days of training lose accuracy sharply in the short term, with the decay stabilising at longer offsets; neither RR nor LSTM generalises well, the LSTM is better at every offset, and both follow a similar decay.
outcomes.source: Section 4.3, paragraph 2; Figure 4D and legend; Discussion, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: LSTM outperformed RR on all days, but both followed a similar decay curve.
outcomes.notes: Under absolute offset and test-day normalisation, the LSTM is above RR at all 101 offsets; LSTM 0.583, 0.376, 0.186 and RR 0.294, 0.088, -0.005 at day 0, 1 to 5 days and 90 to 100 days; normalised curves correlate at r = 0.903. Under the other three pairs the LSTM is also better at every offset, but r is 0.887, 0.526 and 0.391, and with the signed offset and test-day normalisation the sharp-then-stable part fails. With the training day's normalisation RR's mean R2 over the 1-to-5-day and 90-to-100-day offsets is -13.4 to -17.9, and single offsets reach a mean of -436.6. The pass is narrow; the LSTM's early drop exceeds its later drop by 0.017 (0.207 against 0.190) and r exceeds 0.9 by 0.003, over 20 decoders.
deviations: The LSTM is trained on 20 of the 312 sessions (every 16th in date order, chosen before any result), for time; one fit takes 77 to 223 s with four at once, depending on the run (77 s in round 1, 207 to 223 s in round 2; decoding.ipynb prints this run's), so all 312 would take 1.7 to 4.8 hours of fitting, over the 60-minute limit of a notebook.

Both decoders' cross-day curves use the 20 LSTM sessions' decoders, each tested on every session within 100 days (1,088 evaluations per decoder and normalisation), scored on every 5th test bin for time.
The criterion names two readings each of offset and normalisation; the outcome holds under one pair of the four.

outcomes.statement: With neural and behavioural hold-out data shuffled independently on one session, RR gives an average R2 of -0.166 and the LSTM of -0.156.
outcomes.quote: RR had an average R2 of -0.166, and LSTM had an average R2 of -0.156.
outcomes.notes: All shuffles give negative R2. Under reading (a), raw bins permuted, the LSTM median is -0.154 (20 sessions), inside -0.156 +- 0.0156, and RR's -0.223 (312 sessions), outside -0.166 +- 0.0166 (per-session range -0.363 to -0.149). Reading (b) gives -0.410 (RR) and -0.596 (LSTM); whole trials give -0.409 and -0.533. As the paper used one session, single sessions were counted. Under (a) RR is within tolerance on 33 of 312 sessions, and of the 20 LSTM sessions RR is within tolerance on 1, the LSTM on 8 and both on 1; under (b) and whole trials, none.
deviations: The LSTM is trained on 20 of the 312 sessions (every 16th in date order, chosen before any result), for time; one fit takes 77 to 223 s with four at once, depending on the run (77 s in round 1, 207 to 223 s in round 2; decoding.ipynb prints this run's), so all 312 would take 1.7 to 4.8 hours of fitting, over the 60-minute limit of a notebook.
Judged on the median over sessions, as the criterion says, since the paper's one session is not named.

outcomes.statement: Training the LSTM on up to five consecutive past sessions reduces the initial drop in performance within about 5 days of training and improves performance over time, but slightly lowers day-0 performance.
outcomes.quote: Multi-day training, reduced the initial decrease in performance (within ~5 days of training), improving performance over time, but did not seem to impact the longer term decay, and slightly decreases day 0 performance.
outcomes.notes: Over 12 day-0 sessions, five training sessions against one raise mean R2 over relative days 1 to 5 from -0.502 to -0.251, shrink the drop from day 0 from 1.089 to 0.791, and lower day-0 R2 from 0.587 to 0.540 (lower on 11 of 12). R2 after day 0 is negative because input normalisation is held at the training parameters. With the normalisation refit on each test session, the code's variant, the three also hold (days 1 to 5, 0.372 to 0.418; drop 0.215 against 0.086; day 0, 0.587 against 0.503), and R2 after day 0 is positive (mean 0.18 to 0.34 over days 6 to 180), near Figure 5A. 283 day-0 sessions are eligible, as the legend reports, when the last session, with nothing after it, is left out.
deviations: 12 of the 283 day-0 sessions, evenly spaced and chosen before any result, and only 1 and 5 training sessions (the two the criterion compares), for time; the paper trains 1415 LSTMs, 7 to 21 hours here at the 75 to 210 s per fit seen in this attempt's runs.

Scored on every 5th test bin. Of the code's variant of the multi-day trainer, the refit of input normalisation on the test data is run; its 90/10 split and training without noise would need the models retrained and are not.
The last eligible session is left out as it has no later session to test on; this gives the legend's 283.

outcomes.statement: Double-exponential fits to the single-session and five-session conditions over 0 to 180 days show steeper decay for single-session training; the initial decay decreases with more training sessions, but the long-term decay is not significantly affected.
outcomes.quote: A double-exponential fit (Fig. 5A) to the single-session and 5-session conditions over all evaluation sessions (within 180 days of day 0) show steeper decays in the single-session case, confirming our observations... the initial decay decreases with more training sessions, but the long-term decay is not significantly affected.
outcomes.notes: The double-exponential fits to the mean R2 per relative day are degenerate (one session, a component of near-zero amplitude with rate 0.18 and one with rate -0.0029; five sessions, two growing components of opposing amplitude). The initial rate is not more negative for one session and the predicted drop to day 5 is not larger (-0.009 against 0.014). The long-term rates' 95% intervals overlap but are very wide (five sessions, -1.48 to 1.50 per day). Residual RMS 0.40 and 0.65 on a curve that reaches -3.98. With 12 day-0 sessions the curve is likely too noisy for this fit; the raw comparison of fig5a-multiday-short-term does show the smaller early drop with five sessions. Two variants were run after round 1 of the verification. With the test day's normalisation and the criterion's initial values, the initial rate is still not more negative for one session (0.034 against 0.014). Started from the values printed in the Figure 5A panel (negative rates), the fits have lower residuals and all three conditions hold under both normalisations (training day, initial rates -0.906 against -0.182, drop to day 5 1.237 against 0.416, long-term rates -0.0033 and 0.0010 with overlapping intervals; test day, -0.601 against -0.535, drop 0.256 against 0.122, long-term rates -0.0046 and -0.0031, overlapping). In those four fits from the panel's values the initial rates are not well determined, as their 95% intervals include zero and overlap widely (training day -2.09 to 0.28 against -0.62 to 0.25; test day -1.53 to 0.33 against -1.91 to 0.84), so the pass from the panel's values rests on point estimates. The outcome is the criterion's and rests on its initial values, which start from growing components; whether they misread the code is asked of a reader.
deviations: Fit to the 12 day-0 sessions of fig5a-multiday-short-term in place of 283, for time; this may be why the fit fails.

outcomes.statement: Continual daily fine-tuning of an LSTM on 30 s to 5 min of each new session's data, over up to 200 days from 20 seed days, reduces both short- and long-term decay, and with 120 s or 300 s later decoders outperform the day-0 decode.
outcomes.source: Section 4.3, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 5B and legend
outcomes.quote: Fine-tuning with as little as 30 s of data helped reduce both the short and long-term decays in accuracy... In fact, fine-tuning on 120s or 300s led to later decoders outperforming the baseline day 0 decode.
outcomes.notes: The 20 seed days are in the dataset and are followed by 32 to 85 sessions each within 200 days (1146 in all). With the four durations' iterations and the two normalisation readings this is 2,446,600 training iterations, 6.3 hours at the 0.037 s per iteration measured in round 1 with four fits at once, and about 18 hours at round 2's fit times (207 to 223 s per 2000 iterations, about 2.8 times round 1's), beyond the 60-minute notebook limit and the run. The 30 s arm alone (20 seed fits and 1146 fine-tunes of 50 iterations, under both readings) was written as a notebook after round 1 and started in the round-1 revision, but did not finish within that run's time; it is not in the entry, has no output, and supplies no number. The 120 s and 300 s arms on 2 seed days were not started. No part was tested.

findings.statement: ThresholdCrossings is stored with unit volts and conversion 1.0, but it holds integer counts of threshold crossings per 20 ms bin.
The files and the dandiset metadata give the subject's date of birth but not the implant date, so the paper's days after implant (349 to 1591) cannot be recovered from the dataset.

In 81 of 312 files the electrodes table has no imp column at all, in place of empty values; Appendix A.2 says such sessions have no impedance within three weeks, but a column that comes and goes breaks code that reads every file the same way.

The velocity series are described only as velocity of flexion. In the data, velocity at bin t is position at t+1 minus position at t (a forward difference), except at the bin before a pause, so velocity leads position by one bin; the direction of the difference is not stated in the files or the paper.

29 sessions have 72 pauses of 1.05 to 472.9 s between runs of 20 ms bins, which the paper's '(mostly) contiguous' allows but the files do not mark; 998 trials have a length (stop minus start) of at most the 750 ms hold.

The verifier listed the archive's assets and version metadata through the DANDI API with the helper, and tested the helpers on synthetic inputs (circ_median and circ_iqr across the wrap, channel_tuning, participation_ratio, trial_directions), and found them to behave correctly; it found no train/test leakage in decoding (normalisers and output z-scoring fitted on training bins only). It had no attempt record and took the claims from the claims file.

disagreements.reason: signals [27]: the active slope (-1.261e-3) is within tolerance, and inactive channels have lower SBP. The inactive slope is -0.536e-3 against an expected +0.54e-3, so it is outside tolerance under both fit readings. Its size matches to 1% with the opposite sign. The paper prints "0.54 x 10^-3" for inactive channels, calls it "near 0", and says in Section 4.1 that all categories decreased; the claims file reads the value as positive, which suggests a dropped minus sign. Under that reading the claim would be reproduced.

paper_notes.statement: The supplement gives the inactive channels' SBP slope as +0.54e-3 while Section 4.1 says all categories decreased; the data give -0.536e-3, the same size with the main text's sign.

On these data the paper's statements about the two arrays cannot both hold. With the files' array labels, which agree with Figure S1's example (channel 47 medial, row 5, column 5), the lateral bank has the lowest SBP and the shallowest slope, as Appendix C.2 and Figure S4 say, but medial channels are tuned to extension of both fingers and lateral channels to flexion, the reverse of Section 4.2. With the labels swapped the tuning would match and the SBP result would not. Either the tuning description names the arrays the other way round, or its angles use another sign.

In bci_decoding/nn_utils.py, train_model calls add_training_noise(inputs, noise_neural_std, noise_bias_std), whose parameters are (x, bias_neural_std, noise_neural_std), so the code adds a bias of SD 0.1 and white noise of SD 0.2, the reverse of Appendix C.1 (noise 0.1, bias 0.2).

entries.name: temmar-2025
entries.title: Long-term intracortical neural activity and kinematics, LINK (Temmar et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Temmar et al. (2025) on dandiset 001201, which holds 312 sessions of spiking-band power, threshold crossings and finger kinematics from one macaque over 3.5 years. It checks the dataset's counts and contents, the decline of neural signals over time, single-channel tuning, same-day and cross-day decoding with ridge regression and an LSTM, and multi-day training. The LSTM analyses run on subsets of sessions for time, and the continual fine-tuning is too large to run.
